dudley.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of the Black Country
s1loc: Dudley sits at the heart of the Black Country events scene. The Borough Halls run shows across Dudley Town Hall, Stourbridge Town Hall and Halesowen Cornbow Hall, Brierley Hill Civic Hall hosts tributes, live bands and comedy, and the Black Country Living Museum stages 1940s weekends and open-air entertainment. The Black Country Musicom festival fills two stages with music and comedy, while Himley Hall hosts outdoor concerts in its courtyard and Black Country Day spreads events across the borough each summer.

And the trade runs at every size. The bigger halls, festival operators and production companies field large seasonal crews and buy through procurement, while independent event crews, promoters and entertainers around Stourbridge and Halesowen need just a few branded pieces. A workwear supplier here has to serve the museum's living-history weekend and the single crew alike, which is why we run trade accounts for managed reordering and direct online ordering side by side across the wider West Midlands.

The Theatre Royal handles the big touring shows, the UEA LCR brings arena-scale names to campus and the Waterfront covers the alternative gigs, while Norwich Arts Centre is the grassroots room behind the Norwich Sound and Vision festival and EPIC Studios fills out the mid-size circuit. The Norfolk and Norwich Festival, one of the oldest arts festivals in the country, takes over the city for seventeen days each May, and Earlham Park hosts large open-air concerts in summer.
